title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff & regional failover ordering under high load
author: Carmen Ortega
description:
Summary: Production incident (2026-02-18) exposed a race in the SLO enforcer backoff path that could reorder pending failover actions under sustained high load. Symptoms: transient double-failover attempts to the same region, aggressive load-shedding spikes, and oscillation of routing decisions leading to increased P95 latency for affected customers. Impact: intermittent customer-facing latency regressions and excessive capacity churn in multi-region Dedicated clusters. Root cause: the enforcer's backoff queue processing allowed newly-unblocked entries to bypass ordering guarantees when a regional failover event interleaved with a backoff expiry. This caused the regional failover controller to see inconsistent ordering and race on capacity reservation.

This PR fixes the issue by 1) enforcing strict FIFO ordering for backoff queue wakeups relative to pending failover actions, 2) adding a small hysteresis window to regional failover triggers to batch close events and avoid thrash, and 3) exposing new metrics to surface ordering/skew and hysteresis effectiveness. Changes are minimal and intended as a hotfix: the ordering fixes are implemented with a short critical-path lock and a comment/dogfood test demonstrating the race case. The hysteresis value is conservative (100ms default) and is configurable via the SLO enforcer config. Rollout: feature flag gated and deployed to progressive canary groups (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with a health-check gating on P95 latency and failover-rate metrics.
commits_summary: 3 commits: (1) enforcer: serialize backoff wakeup handling to preserve ordering; (2) failover: add hysteresis window and unit tests; (3) tests/docs: add integration sim and release notes
files_changed: services/slo-enforcer/enforcer.go (serialize backoff wakeup handling, add metrics)
pkg/scheduling/backoff.go (refactor queue wake logic, add FIFO guarantees)
docs/operations/slo-enforcer.md (hotfix notes, rollout and config guidance)
review_conversation:
Arjun: Can you explain why FIFO is strictly required? Is there a perf/regress risk from the added lock?
Carmen: The FIFO guarantee prevents newly-unblocked backoff entries from jumping ahead of in-flight failover requests; in practice the lock is held only for the wakeup handoff (~microseconds under normal load). We added microbenchmarks and saw <0.2% P50 regression on a heavy synthetic workload.
Mei: Integration test failed initially (race detected).
Carmen: Fixed - the race was in the test harness; added a barrier in the sim and a deterministic seed. Re-ran CI.
Sophie: Please add a short rollout plan and a kill-switch.
Carmen: Added feature flag and rollout steps to docs; kill-switch is a config toggle and a metrics alert that auto-rolls back to previous behavior if failover_rate increases > 2x baseline within 5m.
Arjun: Approving after CI stable.
Mei: Approving.
Merge: Squash-merged after canaryed on staging and 10% prod for 2 hours with green health checks.
release_notes:
- Hotfix: fix SLO enforcer backoff ordering race that could cause regional failover thrash under load.
- Add 100ms default hysteresis for regional failover triggers (configurable).
- Add metrics: slo_backoff_skew, failover_hysteresis_count.
- Rollout: feature-flag gated; monitored canary rollout performed.
Notes: Recommended to enable on Dedicated clusters first; can be rolled back via SLO_ENFORCER_FAILOVER_HYSTERESIS=0 or the feature flag.
additional_context: Customer impact was observed primarily on Dedicated clusters with cross-region routing enabled. Related Linear: ENG-5982 tracks follow-up to make hysteresis adaptive. Follow-ups: add adaptive hysteresis based on recent failover_rate (ENG-6021) and surface histograms of backoff_skew in Console (PM request).
